note.headline: Stocks grind higher as long yields jump and vol gets sold hard
note.standfirst: The S&P added +0.51% while the 10-year rose 7bp to 5.18%, a split tape where equities ignored a bear steepening move that credit and long duration did not. Positioning into the next session hinges on whether 5.18% on the 10-year holds or extends, because equity breadth and vol compression both look priced for the former.
takeaways: The 10-year yield rose 7bp to 5.18% and the 30-year rose 7bp to 5.47%, a bear steepening move that the equity tape shrugged off.
VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 and VIX9D fell 9.57% to 12.76, pricing near-term calm even as MOVE stayed elevated at 96.0.
Mega-cap tech was split down the middle: MSFT +3.66% and AAPL +1.53% led, META -3.33% and ORCL -1.75% lagged.
Credit diverged from equity risk-on: HYG made a new low on the session and LQD was roughly flat at +0.06%, while EMB was unchanged.
note.desk_view:
The headline indices closed green across the board, Dow +0.93%, S&P +0.51%, Nasdaq 100 +0.42%, Russell 2000 barely positive at +0.07%. Breadth backs the tape: 16 advancers against 9 decliners, a 1.78 ratio. But the composition underneath is not a clean risk-on session. The risk barometer sits at 0.12, dead neutral, and the two biggest positive contributions came from DXY and VIX compressing, not from credit or small caps. HYG and JNK closed down on the day and both hit session lows on the extremes list, alongside long Treasuries and investment grade credit. That is a tape where equity index levels rose while the credit market that funds those same balance sheets sold off. The two do not stay disconnected indefinitely.

The level that decides which read is right is the 10-year at 5.18%. It rose 7bp today on top of a 2s10s curve that steepened 5bp to 31bp, a classic bear steepening pattern where the long end leads. TIPS real yields rose 9bp to 2.85%, so this is not an inflation story, it is a real rate and term premium move. If 10-year yields grind higher from here while equities keep making new highs in mega-cap tech, that gap will close one of two ways: either credit spreads normalize and yields stabilize, validating the equity tape, or higher-for-longer real rates finally bite risk assets and the VIX compression seen today, VIX9D down 9.57%, reverses hard. Watch HYG and LQD tomorrow for the tell.
watching: Whether the 10-year holds above 5.18% or reverses into month-end.
Follow-through in HYG and LQD after today's fresh lows on the credit extremes list.
Mega-cap tech dispersion, META down 3.33% against MSFT up 3.66%, resolving one direction.
VIX and VIX9D compression tested by any rates volatility, given MOVE still at 96.0.
note.equities:
All six major US benchmarks closed positive, led by the Dow at +0.93% and Financials at +0.57%, with Technology the best-performing sector at +0.80%. Breadth confirms the advance at the index level, 16 advancers to 9 decliners, a 1.78 ratio, though dispersion at 1.45 says the gains were not evenly distributed.

The mover list makes that explicit. MSFT (+3.66%) and COST (+2.93%) led, both comfortably ahead of the index. On the other side, META fell 3.33% and Communications was the weakest sector at -0.90%, with ORCL down 1.75% and CRM down 1.76% dragging software names lower even as the broader Technology sector rose. Energy was the other laggard sector, -0.90%, tracking the drop in crude. Small caps barely participated, Russell 2000 +0.07%, a sign the rally stayed concentrated in large-cap winners rather than broadening out.
note.rates:
The curve bear steepened across the board. 2s10s widened 5bp to 31bp, 5s30s widened 3bp to 44bp, and 3m10y widened 2bp to 94bp. Every tenor from 2-year to 30-year rose on the day: 2-year +2bp to 4.87%, 5-year +4bp to 5.03%, 10-year +7bp to 5.18%, 30-year +7bp to 5.47%. The move was led by the long end, consistent with a term premium repricing rather than a front-end policy repricing.

10-year TIPS real yields rose 9bp to 2.85%, the largest single move on the curve sheet, while breakevens were flat to up 1bp across 5-year, 10-year and the 5y5y forward. That combination, real yields doing the work and breakevens static, points to the move being about duration supply and term premium rather than inflation expectations. Long Treasuries (TLT) fell 0.13% and 7-10 year Treasuries (IEF) rose 0.35%, splitting on where along the curve the pain landed.
note.credit: Credit did not confirm the equity rally. US high yield (HYG) fell 0.04% and closed at a session low on the extremes list, alongside JNK down 0.08% and long Treasuries. Investment grade (LQD) was roughly flat at +0.06%, also flagged as a low. EM sovereign USD debt (EMB) was unchanged and printed a session low as well. Leveraged loans (BKLN) were the one pocket of strength, +0.10%. The tone is soft: nothing is breaking down violently, but nothing in credit is confirming the equity strength either.
note.fx: The dollar index fell 0.32% to 100.97, with broad-based dollar weakness against G10: EUR/USD rose 0.23% to 1.14, GBP/USD rose 0.27% to 1.325, AUD/USD rose 0.26% to 0.703. The exception was USD/CHF, up 0.40% to 0.828, and USD/JPY, which fell 1.02% to 157.185, the largest G10 mover and a negative contributor to the risk barometer. In EM, USD/MXN rose 0.77% to 17.676 and USD/BRL rose 0.43%, both dollar-strength moves against the broader DXY softness, while USD/TRY rose 0.13% to 48.916, a fresh high on the extremes list, and USD/INR fell 0.36% to 95.82.
note.commodities: Energy sold off hard: WTI fell 2.33% to 92.41 and Brent fell 2.14% to 104.32, with natural gas down 3.06% to 3.196. Precious metals diverged from the broader risk tape, gold up 0.54% to 4321.2 and silver up 1.24% to 64.245, alongside platinum up 1.46%, while palladium fell 0.51%. Copper fell 0.34% to 6.695. Ags were mixed and quiet: wheat -0.53%, corn +0.14%, soybeans +0.11%.
note.volatility: Vol got sold across the curve. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87, VIX9D fell 9.57% to 12.76, and VIX3M fell 2.71% to 17.93, a curve that steepened as near-term fear came out fastest. VVIX fell 3.01% to 87.84 and SKEW eased 0.77% to 144.91. The one holdout is rates vol: MOVE fell 8.20% on the day but still sits at 96.0, elevated against a 53.945 year-to-date change, keeping the cost of protection in duration well above where equity vol now sits.
note.digital: Bitcoin rose 0.18%, essentially flat and showing little beta to the equity rally or the dollar's decline. Ether fell 0.13%, Solana fell 0.52%, and XRP fell 2.75%, the weakest of the majors. Digital assets traded like a market waiting for a catalyst rather than one following risk sentiment.
note.international: Asia was split. Nikkei rose 1.30% to a fresh high while Hang Seng fell 1.01% and TAIEX fell 0.28%, also flagged as a high on the extremes list despite the daily decline. KOSPI rose 0.90%. Europe closed broadly firm: EURO STOXX 50 +0.48%, DAX +0.56%, IBEX +0.65%, FTSE MIB +0.63%, with CAC the lone laggard at -0.05%. The handoff to New York was a session with rising equities and a weaker dollar already in train before the US cash open, both themes that carried through the US session.
note.correlation:
The standard playbook, equities up and vol down together, held today, VIX -5.11% against S&P +0.51%. What did not hold is the usual credit confirmation: HYG and LQD both sat at session lows while equities rose, and the risk barometer's largest positive contributions came from DXY and VIX, not from HYG, EMB, or the Russell 2000, which contributed next to nothing at +0.07.

That gap between equity price action and credit tone is the thing to watch. If it closes with credit catching up to equity strength, the current pattern is just noise. If it closes the other way, with equities catching down to credit softness and rising real yields, the vol compression seen today reverses quickly given MOVE is still sitting at 96.0. A break would show up first as HYG making new lows while VIX9D stops falling.
